title: Coefficient constants rigidity
statement: Let $A\hookrightarrow B$ be an injective local map of complete discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], with fraction fields $K\subseteq L$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Local means that the inverse image of the maximal ideal is the maximal ideal. Suppose $\mathfrak m_AB=\mathfrak m_B$ and $K$ has characteristic zero. Put $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$ and $l=B/\mathfrak m_B$, and assume $\operatorname{char}(k)=p>0$, with $p$ prime, and $k=\bigcap_{r\geq0}l^{p^r}$ inside $l$, where $l^{p^r}=\{x^{p^r}:x\in l\}$. Then $k$ is perfect (the map $x\mapsto x^p$ on $k$ is surjective), and every element of $L$ algebraic over $K$ belongs to $K$. Here algebraic means satisfying a nonzero polynomial with coefficients in $K$. In particular, every root of unity in $B$ belongs to $A$.

source.place: Tag 09E8, remark-finite-separable-extension (degree equals ramification index times residue degree for a complete DVR), and the perfect-core hypothesis in Tag 09F5, lemma-lowering-the-level. The constants-rigidity deduction used to descend zeta is supplied by the worker.

proof.text: First prove that $k$ is perfect. For $a\in k$, the perfect-core hypothesis gives $b\in l$ with $b^p=a$. For every $r\geq0$ it also gives $c\in l$ with $c^{p^{r+1}}=a$. Injectivity of Frobenius in the field $l$ implies $b=c^{p^r}$. Thus $b\in\bigcap_r l^{p^r}=k$, as required. Injectivity here follows directly from $(x-y)^p=x^p-y^p$ in characteristic $p$ and the absence of nonzero nilpotents in a field.

source.place: Tag 09F5, lemma-lowering-the-level, perfect-core hypothesis and the proof sentence asserting perfectness; explicit elementary verification.

proof.text: Fix $x\in L$ algebraic over $K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension], $E=K(x)\subseteq L$ is finite over $K$. Let $C\subseteq E$ be the integral closure of $A$: its elements satisfy monic polynomials over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. The DVR $A$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] and complete, so by [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-nagata] applied to the prime $0$ the domain $A$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]: $C$ is a finite $A$-module. As $C\subseteq E$ is a domain, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product] makes $C$ a Noetherian complete local ring whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_C$ is the only prime over $\mathfrak m_A$. $A$ is a Noetherian local domain of dimension one with $\mathfrak m_A\ne0$ [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one], so [lem-sfb-finite-normalization-local-dvr] gives a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $C$ over $\mathfrak m_A$, hence $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak m_C$, and says $\{c/s:s\notin\mathfrak m_C\}$ is a DVR with fraction field $E$ and maximal ideal meeting $A$ in $\mathfrak m_A$. Elements of $C\setminus\mathfrak m_C$ are units of the local ring $C$, so this subring is $C$ itself: $C$ is a complete DVR, finite over $A$, with fraction field $E$, and $A\to C$ is local. Since $B$ is a PID by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] makes $B$ integrally closed in $L$. Every $c\in C$ satisfies its monic equation also over $B$, so $c\in B$. Hence $A\subseteq C\subseteq B$ inside $L$.

source.place: Tag 09E8, remark-finite-separable-extension, finite normalization; Tags 09EM, remark-construction (4),(8), and 09F8, lemma-special-case, proof first paragraph, complete DVR normalization. Simple-field finiteness: Fields Tag 09GH. Finiteness and locality of the normalization: algebra.tex Tag 032W (lemma-Noetherian-complete-local-Nagata) and Tag 0325 (lemma-quotient-complete-local).

proof.text: Choose uniformizers $\pi$ of $A$ and $t$ of $C$. The DVRs are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] in $C$ to write $\pi=u t^e$ with $u\in C^\times$. Localness of $A\to C$ gives $e\geq1$. The image of $\pi$ generates $\mathfrak m_B$ by hypothesis, so it is not a unit of $B$; since $u$ remains a unit, $t$ is not a unit of $B$ either. If $e\geq2$, then $\pi\in\mathfrak m_B^2=\pi^2B$, contradicting cancellation of the nonzero $\pi$ (which would make $\pi$ a unit). Thus $e=1$ and $\mathfrak m_C=tC=\pi C$. Moreover $C\to B$ is local: a unit of $C$ stays a unit of $B$, and every nonunit of $C$ is a multiple of $t\in\mathfrak m_B$. The residue map $h=C/\mathfrak m_C\to l$ is consequently injective and compatible with $k\to l$.

source.place: Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr, unit-times-uniformizer-power description; direct cancellation using the weakly unramified hypothesis.

proof.text: Identify $h=C/\mathfrak m_C$ with its image in $l$. Since $\mathfrak m_C=\mathfrak m_AC$, the images of any finite set of $A$-module generators of $C$ span $h$ over $k$. Hence $h/k$ is finite-dimensional and algebraic: for each $a\in h$, sufficiently many of $1,a,a^2,\ldots$ are linearly dependent, giving a nonzero polynomial over $k$ that vanishes at $a$. Step 1 and [lem-per-algebraic-extension-perfect] therefore imply that $h$ is perfect. For $a\in h$ and every $r$, iterating surjectivity of Frobenius on $h$ gives $b\in h\subseteq l$ with $b^{p^r}=a$. Thus $h\subseteq\bigcap_r l^{p^r}=k$. Since $k\subseteq h$ via the residue map, $h=k$, with their specified embeddings in $l$.

source.place: Algebra.IsAlgebraic.perfectField, lines 343-347, applied to the finite residue extension; the inclusions into the perfect core are the explicit elementary argument.

proof.text: The finite $A$-module $C$ satisfies $C/\mathfrak m_AC=h=k$, and the class of $1\in C$ spans this quotient over $k$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] to $M=C$ and the single generator $1$. Its hypotheses hold because $A$ is local and $C$ is finite over $A$ by step 2. It follows that $C=A\cdot1=A$ as subrings of $L$.

source.place: Tag 00DV, lemma-NAK (8): lift the single residue generator 1.

proof.text: Taking fraction fields of $C=A$ gives $E=K$. Since $x\in E$, the arbitrary element $x\in L$ algebraic over $K$ lies in $K$. This proves the entire algebraic-constants assertion, not just its root-of-unity consequence.

source.place: Tag 09E8, remark-finite-separable-extension; elementary conclusion of the finite-normalization argument.

proof.text: Let $\zeta\in B$ satisfy $\zeta^n=1$ for some integer $n\geq1$. The polynomial $T^n-1$ is nonzero and monic over $A$, so $\zeta$ is algebraic over $K$ and step 6 gives $\zeta\in K$. The same monic equation makes it integral over $A$. By [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] $A$ is a PID, and [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] says precisely that every such element of its fraction field belongs to $A$. Thus $\zeta\in A$.
